headline: High risk of shared-repo prompt injection and cascading errors; Langflow’s default server-side flows amplify Aider’s repo edits.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files in a shared repo, while Langflow can ingest uploaded files and chain tools in flows. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Langflow outputs are copied into the repo or consumed as trusted text. The pathway is not proven by docs alone, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF Langflow flow output is written into the shared repo and then read by Aider as trusted text, injection risk materializes.
IF either agent parses the other’s generated text as instructions without provenance checks, the attack path exists.
mitigations: Keep Langflow outputs out of the repo; use a separate staging directory.
Add a manual review step before Aider consumes any Langflow-generated text.
Prefix all flow outputs with non-executable delimiters and strip instructions.
Use separate OS users or containers for the two agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/content separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history, and Langflow handles flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and server-side files. If they share a workspace or uploaded files, sensitive code can flow into Langflow’s broader API-connected environment. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace by default, so medium is the highest justified severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem or repo checkout, code and history can be exposed to Langflow.
IF Langflow components send uploaded file contents to configured model providers or HTTP services, those contents can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Use separate repositories or bind mounts for each agent.
Disable file uploads in Langflow for sensitive projects.
Restrict Langflow components to local-only providers.
Rotate or redact secrets before either agent sees the workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies at the orchestrator boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the filesystem and modify git state; Langflow can also write the filesystem and run unsandboxed Python code by default. Both therefore have overlapping write authority over shared mutable resources, and Aider explicitly shares state via a shared git repo. That matches the high-risk conflict pattern in the rubric.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repo or directory, concurrent writes can clobber each other.
IF Langflow Python components mutate files while Aider is committing, git state corruption or lost edits can occur.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate working trees.
Serialize write access with a lock file or queue.
Disable Langflow file-writing components for shared repos.
Have Aider commit only after Langflow finishes a flow.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is designed to chain multiple agents and tools, while Aider produces code edits and git commits. If Langflow consumes Aider’s output as authoritative, downstream flow nodes can amplify a mistaken patch into broader actions. Because the pairwise interaction is undocumented and both are open-ended, I choose high over medium under the uncertainty rule.
conditions: IF Langflow treats Aider-generated code or summaries as verified facts, downstream actions can propagate errors.
IF a Langflow flow triggers API calls or file writes based on Aider output, the error blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require human approval before Langflow acts on Aider output.
Insert a verification step that re-reads source files before execution.
Limit Langflow flows to read-only analysis when fed by Aider.
Log and diff all Aider edits before downstream use.
requires-engineering: add schema validation and confidence gating between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles model-provider API keys and git history, while Langflow stores per-flow credentials and can send data to arbitrary HTTP services. If regulated or sensitive code is processed in a shared deployment, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium fits the documented policy gap.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or secrets are routed through Langflow flows, retention and third-party transfer obligations apply.
IF the deployment stores Aider git history and Langflow flow state under different retention policies, compliance mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Avoid sending secrets through either agent.
Align retention settings for git history and flow logs.
Document which data classes each agent may process.
Use region-locked providers where required.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for residency and retention.
